hook.desc: Extreme close-up of muddy running shoes hitting wet pavement at dawn, no music, only footsteps

per_ad.visual_pattern: Fast cuts every 1.2s in first 10s, slows to 3s cuts at emotional peak (t=28), product logo appears bottom-right at t=45, full-screen CTA at t=58

hook.desc: Split-screen: child kicking a ball on a dirt field / pro athlete in a stadium — mirrored motion

per_ad.visual_pattern: Split-screen held for 8s, merges at t=9, black-and-white palette until t=22 when color floods in, logo appears t=52

hook.desc: Black screen, single heartbeat sound, then athlete's face in extreme close-up — eyes only

per_ad.visual_pattern: Minimal cuts for first 15s (slow build), explosion of rapid 0.5s cuts t=15–30, single static hero shot at t=45, wordless CTA at t=60

patterns.insight: All three ads open with a sensory-first hook (sound or extreme close-up) before any branding — viewer is emotionally committed before they know it's Nike
The tagline 'Just Do It' appears only in the final 5 seconds across all ads — it functions as a seal, not an opener
Emotional arc always passes through a struggle or contrast phase before resolution — conflict is structural, not optional
Logo placement is consistently late and small — brand confidence expressed through restraint

gap: Nike never shows failure as permanent — every arc resolves upward. No ad sits with doubt, exhaustion, or quitting as the final emotion. The brand avoids the athlete who stops.

counter_creative.angle: Celebrate the athlete who stopped — and came back on their own terms, not Nike's
counter_creative.script: Open on an empty pair of running shoes by a front door. Voiceover: 'I stopped for two years.' Cut to ordinary life — commute, desk, couch. No shame, no struggle music. Then: shoes laced up again, no fanfare, just a walk that becomes a jog. End frame: 'Whenever you're ready.' No 'Just Do It.' Brand logo only. — This exploits the gap by owning the pause Nike never acknowledges, making the brand feel human rather than relentless.
